summary:
# NOTES: "Strong Poison" by Dorothy L. Sayers (1930), single book

## Front matter / epigraph
- Old ballad "Lord Rendal": "Where gat ye your dinner, Lord Rendal, my son?"; reply: dined with sweetheart; "Oh that was strong poison"; "I am poisoned, Mother; make my bed soon."

## CHAPTER I (trial, Old Bailey-style; judge elderly, parrot-faced, scarlet robe; crimson roses on bench)
- Judge sums up. Explains presumption of innocence, "reasonable doubt" = doubt as in everyday business; not 4 a.m. nightmare doubts.
- Jury: tall argumentative tradesman; stout embarrassed tradesman with drooping moustache; unhappy man with cold; company director; publican; two artisan youths; nondescript elderly educated man; artist with red beard/weak chin; elderly spinster (later Miss Climpson); sweet-shop keeper stout woman; harassed wife/mother.
- Salcombe Hardy (reporter, drowned-violet eyes) and Waffles Newton: "Judge hostile."
- Accused: **Harriet Vane**, 29, novelist of detective/mystery stories; brought up strictly religious; orphaned/left at 23.
- Victim: **Philip Boyes**, 36, writer, five novels, essays; "advanced" views (atheism, anarchy, free love).
- Met 1927 in artistic/literary circles. Lived together ~1928 after March 1928 (she gave in). Quarrel Feb 1929; she left next day (Dyer couple upstairs heard quarrel). Reason: Boyes offered legal marriage; she was angry ("made a fool of her").
- Witnesses named: Sylvia Marriott, Eiluned Price (friends), Mr. and Mrs. Dyer, Mr. Norman Urquhart (cousin, solicitor, Woburn Square), Mr. Ryland Vaughan (friend), Dr. Green, Dr. Weare, Dr. Grainger, Sir James Lubbock, Stephen Fordyce (analysts), Mr. Brown (chemist, Southampton Row).
- Counsel: Sir Impey Biggs (defence); Attorney-General (prosecution); Mr. Crofts of Crofts & Cooper (defence solicitors). Judge later named Crossley; next judge Bancroft.
- Freddy Arbuthnot (Hon.) and Lord Peter Wimsey in gallery; Dowager Duchess of Denver (mother), who notes Miss Climpson on jury.
- Purchases: **10 April**, arsenic 2 oz at Brown's, Southampton Row, signed "Mary Slater" (handwriting = Vane); said for rats (no rats in flats). **5 May**, arsenical weed-killer, name "Edith Waters". Other poisons: prussic acid, strychnine; aconitine attempt. Commercial arsenic coloured with charcoal/indigo.
- Vane's explanation: writing novel about poisoning (publisher **Mr. Trufoot**; book titled *Death in the Pot*); Challoner (agent) testifies she discussed poison book in December.
- Boyes' gastric attacks: **31 March**, **15 April**, **12 May** (Dr. Weare's case-book, 1925 earlier attack).
- Meetings: late March, second week April, some time May.
- Boyes in Harlech (Wales) with Vaughan after May; letter to Harriet **16 June**: "Life is an utter mess-up... cut adrift and take a trip out West... I shall be in town on the 20th." Reply: "You can come round at 9.30 on the 20th... you certainly will not make me change my mind." Signed "M."
- Urquhart says "out West" = voyage to Barbados.

## Death day: 20 June
- Boyes back from Wales 19 June with Vaughan. Breakfast bacon/eggs; 11 am Guinness ("Good for you"); lunch at club; tennis.
- 7:30 to Urquhart's house, Woburn Square. Dinner 8 pm exactly, library sherry (Oloroso 1847, decanted), maid **Hannah Westlock**, cook **Mrs. Pettican**.
- Menu: cold bouillon (jellied); turbot with sauce; poulet en casserole; sweet omelette made by Boyes in chafing-dish from 4 eggs broken by Urquhart into bowl with sugar; jam brought by Hannah. Burgundy (Corton) only Boyes drank (two glasses); bottle preserved, found harmless. Urquhart abstained ("advised not to drink at mealtimes").
- 9:15 Boyes taxi to **100 Doughty Street** (Harriet's flat). PC D.1234 saw him ringing 9:25. Mrs. Bright ground floor.
- Harriet: offered coffee "standing ready upon the gas-ring"; earlier statement "a cup of coffee ready for him."
- ~10 pm argument; Boyes felt unwell, said behaviour upset him.
- 10:10 taxi-driver **Burke** at Guilford Street rank; Boyes to Woburn Square, doubled over, "Yes, rotten."
- Hannah opened door; brandy-and-soda; Urquhart: "Hullo, old man"; Boyes: "It can't have been the chicken."
- Dr. Grainger called; diagnosed acute gastritis; mixture: bicarbonate of potash, tincture of oranges, chloroform. Dr. Weare consulted next day.

## CHAPTER II
- Nurse Williams (nurse from 21 June). 22 June: Boyes' father Rev. Arthur Boyes present; Boyes said "I'm going out, Dad... Harriet'll be rid of me now--I didn't know she hated me quite so much." Died 3 am **23 June**. Funeral **28 June**.
- Nurse Williams gossiped at another patient's house (Bloomsbury circle), mentioned arsenic; Miss Marriott, Miss Price, Vaughan heard. Vaughan told Urquhart; Urquhart consulted Weare; Vaughan wrote to elder Mr. Boyes; exhumation.
- Analysis: four or five grains arsenic ~3 days before death; hair arsenic near roots (~10 weeks growth; ~3 months before death). Quarrel Feb → 5 months to death; first illness March → 4 months.
- Defence: ten unaccounted minutes (9:50–10:10) maybe suicide or pub. Prosecution: no evidence Boyes had arsenic.
- Police: Vane said "Arsenic? What an extraordinary thing!" Burnt poisons before end of May. Flat searched, nothing.
- Chal­loner evidence: book on poisons discussed December; her shelves had Madeleine Smith, Seddon, Armstrong trials.
- Summing-up: "The prisoner had the means... the expert knowledge... the opportunity."

## CHAPTER III
- Jury out 1.5 h+ ; 6.5 h total. Foreman (irritable; wants agreement); elderly spinster (Climpson) holds out. Verdict: **disagreement**; retrial later (discharged, "excused from jury service for 12 years").
- Wimsey catches Biggy; Miss Climpson hugs... kisses (Wimsey proposes).
- Chief-Inspector Charles Parker (Wimsey's friend, believes case).

## CHAPTER IV (Sunday; council at Biggy's)
- Juror reports: Climpson (High-Church, tough); sweet-shop woman (dislikes foreman, believes Vane may have done it? backs Climpson); artist (believes Vane, suspects suicide).
- Costs borne by publishers and newspaper running serial. Wimsey pays secretly.
- Wimsey at **Holloway** Gaol with Harriet: "Sit down." Proposes; she refuses ("forty-seven proposals"). Her lines: "couldn't stand being made a fool of... matrimony offered as a bad-conduct prize." Wimsey's hobbies: first editions, incunabula; brother takes estate; mother = Dowager Duchess; Bunter = manservant. Wimsey: "I've got a silly face."
- Wimsey: "thirty-one days" (window bill GREAT SPECIAL OFFER).

## CHAPTER V (Miss Katharine Climpson's typing bureau = "the Cattery")
- Staff: spinsters, widows; Scotland Yard line; Wimsey's bank pays.
- Motives discussed: passion, jealousy, money (insurance, inheritance), blackmail, suicide (arsenic "tomfool"). Duc de Praslin mentioned.
- Dates: Michaelmas Term ends 21st (Dec); "this is the 15th"; Hilary term starts **January 12th**.
- Parker: Wimsey asks check: pub near Doughty St 9:50–10:10; bottle or paper; garden in **Mecklenburgh Square**.
- Wimsey's sister issue: Wimsey mentions Parker "went off the deep end about my sister" (Lady Mary).

## CHAPTER VI
- Wimsey's car "Mrs. Merdle". Visits Rev. Arthur Boyes at **Tweedling Parva** vicarage. Letters from Philip: "Your morality will be pleased... regularise the situation"; "Harriet has succeeded in making a fool of herself and me." Will: Philip's copyrights left to **Vaughan**; earlier will left everything to Harriet. Great-aunt **Cremorna Garden** (actress, 1860s, alive, 90+, childish) — father's wife's aunt.
- Wimsey donates treasury notes to church box.
- Publisher **Mr. Cole** (Grimsby & Cole): boom in sales; Wimsey asks First Edition.
- Agent **Mr. Challoner**: Harriet's book *Death in the Pot*; galleys.

## CHAPTER VII
- Wimsey at Holloway: will—Harriet was named beneficiary; she didn't know of change. Plot talk (fiction) about killing for will; deed-of-gift idea.
- Visits Urquhart's house: cook (stout elderly woman, unnamed; parlour-maid in bed with influenza). Urquhart away in **Windle, Westmorland**, care of **Mrs. Wrayburn**, Appleford. Office: Bedford Row.
- Head-clerk **Mr. Pond**. Telephone to Miss Climpson: vacancy for clerk at Urquhart's office.

## CHAPTER VIII
- Bunter (valet). Bunter hints at romance (Hannah?); Wimsey says "I'm being obvious."
- Marjorie Phelps (porcelain figurine maker; Wimsey's ex, "Bellona Club affair"). Bohemian party at **Kropotkys'** (Nina, Vanya, Stanislas, Boris, Marya; Vrilovitch). Ryland Vaughan: "that bitch of a woman poisoned him"; shows small bottle of poison in breast-pocket ("waiting"); Phil talked of "ivory gate"; Urquhart a "sleek family lawyer".
- Joey Trimbles' studio. Sylvia Marriott sprained ankle; Eiluned Price (short, stout, pugnacious nose). Sylvia suspects Urquhart ("doesn't like the way he does his hair").
- Parker's call: pub found; white powder packet to be found.

## CHAPTER IX (Bunter at Urquhart's kitchen tea)
- Cook **Mrs. Pettican**; **Hannah Westlock** (Wednesday off/Friday off / every other Sunday). Eggs: one cracked, Urquhart put it into bowl. Burgundy corked, sealed with plaster, initialled by Hannah. Mrs. Wrayburn was actress "'Yde Park" / Cremorna Garden; children died in cholera. Urquhart's train 6:30.

## CHAPTER X
- **Mrs. Bulfinch** (Gracie; formerly Miss Montague, barmaid, the Nine Rings, Gray's Inn Road; husband Bulfinch; barman George). Night ~June 20, ~10:05 pm: young man (Boyes) gasped "Give me a double brandy"; said "I'm subject to gastric trouble"; drank white powder packet in water, stirred with fountain-pen. Packet left behind, put on shelf behind bar.
- Wimsey at Urquhart's Bedford Row office. Urquhart: cousin Philip; Mrs. Wrayburn; Urquhart is legatee ("I am the legatee myself"); Philip asked about money 18 months ago. Claims will in safe at home; deed-box "Wrayburn".

## CHAPTER XI
- Urquhart's family history: grandparents Hubbard; Jane (Brown); Mary (Urquhart, lace-trade); Rosanna (Cremorna Garden). Will text: estate to Norman for life, then issue; **Philip Boyes gets nothing**; "inhuman treatment". Typewriter: Woodstock with chipped lower-case p, misaligned A.
- Harriet & Wimsey talk: "Barbara" (old flame); "Barbara celarent darii ferio baralipton."
- Note from **Joan Murchison** (typist at Urquhart's): Megatherium Trust. Same Woodstock typewriter, chipped p, misaligned A.

## CHAPTER XII (Christmas at Duke's Denver)
- Guests: Mrs. "Freak" Dimsworthy, Captain Tommy Bates, Mrs. Featherstone, Miss Titterton, Harringay, Helen (Duchess, Wimsey's sister-in-law), Duke Gerald, Freddy Arbuthnot (engaged to Rachel Levy), Lady Mary Wimsey.
- Lady Mary & Wimsey: Wimsey urges Parker to propose to Mary.

## CHAPTER XIII
- Miss Murchison (38, plain) visits Wimsey's flat; Bach; Blindfold Bill Rumm (ex-burglar, Whitechapel Road, Salvation-style meeting, wife Bella, daughter Esmeralda Hyacinth). Lock-picking lesson. Wimsey instructs: find real will/trust; Urquhart typed on machine 3 years old.

## CHAPTER XIV
- Murchison stays late; takes deed-box WRAYBURN; finds Deed of Trust (July 1920) and letter from Rosanna Wrayburn 15 May 1920; securities list. Mr. Pond returns; caviare; mouse.

## CHAPTER XV
- Lunch at Rules. Wimsey despair; sends Miss Climpson to Windle. Parker report: packet found = **bicarbonate of soda**.

## CHAPTER XVI
- Climpson letter from Hillside View (Windle), 1 Jan 1930; boarding house (Mrs. Pegler, Miss Etheredge, Miss Tweall, Mrs. Liffey); Mrs. Wrayburn's house on Kendal Road; nurse **Miss Caroline Booth**; stout nurse in black veil; Oriental Café; spiritualism; Mrs. Craig; "Pongo" control; Harry, Mabel, Ellen Pate.

## CHAPTER XVII–XVIII
- Séances; Miss Booth; will search; Cremorna Garden communications ("Norman... wants it"); safe combination from black note-book (12, 18, 4, 0, 9, 3, 15); will found in safe.

## CHAPTER XIX
- Climpson reads will (estate to Philip Boyes; £50,000 cash to Philip; residue to Norman Urquhart as sole executor); letter to Wimsey (7 Jan 1930).

## CHAPTER XX
- Mr. Pond/Urquhart; Murchison finds hidden panel behind mantelpiece: securities misappropriated (Megatherium); white arsenic packet. Council at 110a Piccadilly; Marsh's test confirms arsenic.

## CHAPTER XXI–XXII
- Harriet refuses marriage ("I'll live with you"). Manicurist (kitten-faced) cuts parings/hair for samples.
- Wimsey interviews Urquhart: egg theory; arsenic immunity (Styrian peasants); Urquhart taking arsenic medicine; Urquhart eats marzipan/Turkish delight laced with arsenic (Wimsey's claim); Urquhart arrested by Parker.

## CHAPTER XXIII
- Charge against Vane withdrawn; verdict Not Guilty. Eiluned & Sylvia greet her. Wimsey goes to Duke's Denver; tells Duke he intends "to marry the prisoner... if she'll have me."
